questions.q: When a user requests a self-requestable role, what happens immediately?
options: The role is provisioned to their account instantly, with no further steps
The request routes to an approval workflow, and the role is only provisioned once approved
Nothing — self-requestable roles cannot actually be requested
The role mapping itself is deleted
questions.explain: A self-requested role still has to clear an approval workflow before it is actually provisioned to the user's account.

questions.q: At Castellan Robotics, why does an Accounts Payable Specialist's role request route to the AP Supervisor rather than to the requester's own manager?
options: To avoid a self-approving arrangement if that manager also holds conflicting access, such as payment approval
Because the AP Supervisor is always the fastest approver available
Because managers are never allowed to approve any requests
Because the Security Console requires all approvals to go through a supervisor by default
questions.explain: Choosing an approver deliberately, rather than defaulting to the requester's manager, helps avoid the kind of segregation-of-duties conflict covered in Lesson 13.

questions.q: How is a higher-risk role that is NOT marked self-requestable typically requested?
options: It can never be requested or granted under any circumstances
Automatically, the same way as any self-requestable role
Only by the user editing their own account directly
Through a formal request (ticket, form, or similar) reviewed against actual job need and provisioned manually once approved
questions.explain: Roles not marked self-requestable require a formal, manual request process outside of self-service, reviewed and provisioned by an administrator.

questions.q: Why does the extra friction around requesting higher-risk, non-self-requestable roles exist?
options: It's an unintended flaw in Oracle Fusion that implementers should try to remove
It only exists because of a software bug
It's an intentional control, ensuring higher-risk access gets more scrutiny than routine access
It has nothing to do with security and is purely cosmetic
questions.explain: The extra friction for higher-risk roles is deliberate: it ensures sensitive access receives more scrutiny than roles that can be safely self-requested.

questions.q: Why does documenting every access request and approval matter, even when the access turns out to be entirely appropriate?
options: It doesn't matter at all if the access was appropriate
The documentation is the evidence auditors rely on to answer 'why does this person have this access'; a lack of it can itself be flagged as a finding
Documentation is only required for roles that were denied
Oracle Fusion automatically generates this documentation with no action needed
questions.explain: Audits rely on documented justification for access; even appropriate access without documentation can be flagged as a finding because the reasoning can't be verified.
